narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the organization has decided to deny your promotion.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. First, your overall career experience of 6-10 years was the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. Employees predicted to stay are more likely to have either very short (1-5 years) or much longer experience, so your mid-range tenure stands out as a risk for turnover. Second, the fact that you have not received other job offers while at the company worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward staying. Finally, having spent 1-5 years in your current role added further weight toward leaving, as this tenure pattern is less common among those the model expects to remain.

Taken together, these elements created a slight tilt toward predicting departure. The organization should consider discussing your long-term career goals with you and exploring whether additional responsibilities or clearer growth paths could increase your commitment. You may want to reflect on what would make staying more attractive or whether external opportunities better match your ambitions at this stage.
